Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

imply verb

suggest without saying

also hint, insinuate, what are you implying?, it follows that

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.3.213: hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est (Lewis & Short)

significō, significāre, significāvī, significātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

give to understand, intimate, hint

To show by a sign rather than say outright (Lewis & Short: “to intimate, notify”); of a word, to mean (see mean). The noun is significātiō (see implication).

Other words

  • sequitur ut — it follows that (logically)

    sequor, sequī, impersonal, with ut + subjunctive or an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fat. 28 (Lewis & Short)

    For “this implies that” in an argument: the conclusion follows (see involve for “entail”).

Examples

  • hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est

    he seemed to hint this to me and nodCic. Verr. 2.3.213 (Lewis & Short)

  • sī haec ēnūntiātiō vēra nōn est, sequitur, ut falsa sit

    if this statement is not true, it follows that it is falseCic. Fat. 28 (Lewis & Short)

See also mean, implication, suggest, involve.

SourcesLewis & Short: significo · Lewis & Short: sequor

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
